candidates.lead: Australian income tax brackets for 2020-21 through 2023-24 were 0% to $18,200, 19% to $45,000, 32.5% to $120,000, 37% to $180,000 and 45% above [[PRE_STAGE3]]. The revised Stage 3 cuts from 1 July 2024 changed them to 16% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000 and 45% above [[POST_STAGE3]], and from 1 July 2026 the 16% rate fell to 15% [[TAX_BRACKETS_2026_27]].

The 2023 tax brackets (financial years 2022-23 and 2023-24) taxed residents at 19% on $18,201–$45,000, 32.5% on $45,001–$120,000, 37% on $120,001–$180,000 and 45% above $180,000, with no tax on the first $18,200 [[PRE_STAGE3]]. Those thresholds had applied unchanged since 2020-21; the Stage 3 restructure replaced them from 1 July 2024 [[POST_STAGE3]].

Tax bracket history in Australia has three phases since 2020: four years of the 19%/32.5%/37%/45% scale to June 2024 [[PRE_STAGE3]]; the Stage 3 scale of 16%/30%/37%/45% with a $135,000 middle threshold from 1 July 2024 [[POST_STAGE3]]; and the 2026-27 scale that cuts the 16% rate to 15% on $18,201–$45,000 from 1 July 2026 [[TAX_BRACKETS_2026_27]]. The 2% Medicare levy sits on top in every year.
